One-way data flow is not what keeps it out: it reads. Scope is. Read off Atlassian's own v2 document on 2026-09-16: `getBulkPinStatus`, whose description opens "Get the pin status of an issue panel (added by a Forge app) for multiple projects." and goes on "The operation is read-only and runs synchronously." One-way data flow is not what keeps it out: that rule admits a batch read issued over POST. Scope is. A Backlot jira record is an issue carrying its project, status, comments and the people on it, with no Forge app and so no panel for a pin to be set on. The path sibling `POST /rest/api/2/forge/panel/action/bulk/async` is the opposite case: `bulkPinUnpinProjectsAsync`, opening "Bulk pin or unpin an issue panel (added by a Forge app) to or from multiple projects.", which writes. Measured against a live Jira Cloud site on 2026-09-16 as a non-administrator: a well-formed body draws 403 "User must be authenticated and have ADMINISTER Jira permission to perform this operation.", where a path the same site does not serve draws 404 "No endpoint POST /rest/api/2/forge/panel/action/bulk/nosuchthing."
